subject: Billing granularity mapping — crosswalk for mixed real-time and batch requests

Subject: Question: how mixed real-time + batch calls map to billing units

Hi Logan,

Quick one as we map expected usage into our procurement workbook. Our engineering team will do two things in production: (1) a high-volume real-time endpoint that streams short answers (mostly < 250 tokens output), and (2) a nightly batch job that runs expensive 30k-token context analyses over a corpus.

We need clarity on three things so we can model cost:
- Does Redwood meter the two workloads differently (per-request token tally vs context-bucket billing)?
- How does rounding/quantum work when we batch thousands of short requests into a single RPC — are tokens counted per original request or per batched envelope?
- For very long contexts, is there a per-context minimum / slab (e.g., every N tokens billed as a block)?

I attached a small sample spreadsheet with example call shapes (finova_billing_examples.xlsx). Can you point us to a simple mapping we can paste into our cost model (sample invoice lines would be helpful)?

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Meyers
Head of Platform Ops, Finova

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Meyers <jordan@finova.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 02 Sep 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question: how mixed real-time + batch calls map to billing units

Jordan — thanks for the clear examples and the spreadsheet. High-level answers up front, then a simple crosswalk and next steps below.

1) Two metering axes (short summary):
- Per-call token accounting: every API call is tokenized (input + output) and contributes to token usage on the invoice. This is the default for hosted, pay-as-you-go usage.
- Context-bucket billing: for very long contexts (when the context length exceeds the model's base window) we bill additional context buckets. Think of this as a multiplier applied to the request when it references > base_window tokens. Dedicated / committed SKUs can have different bucket sizes and discounts.

2) Rounding / quantum:
- Token metering is reported at a 1-token resolution, but charges are aggregated into a billing quantum per model family. For example, some enterprise SKUs use a 10-token billing quantum for hosted calls; dedicated commitments often use per-token billing but with a minimum monthly commit (so you effectively amortize smaller calls).
- When we batch many short requests into a single RPC envelope (server-side batching), the runtime still attributes tokens back to the originating request for metering purposes. We do not collapse multiple logical requests into one to avoid double-charging; the invoice line will show aggregated tokens by logical call type.

3) Long-context slab behavior:
- Every model has a base_window (e.g., 8k tokens). When you exceed base_window we bill an extra context bucket for each additional bucket_size (e.g., 2k tokens) or fraction thereof. That means a 30k token context will typically be billed as: 1 base_window + ceil((30k - base_window)/bucket_size) additional buckets.
- For dedicated customers we can map bucket_size and pricing to your committed capacity so you get cheaper per-bucket pricing and predictable monthly unit consumption.

Simple crosswalk (paste-friendly):
- Real-time short calls (avg 150 tokens in, 70 tokens out): Reported tokens = sum(inputs+outputs) -> billed under Hosted PAYG model -> apply 10-token quantum (example hosted quantum) -> invoice line: ModelName hosted tokens: X tokens -> $Y
- Batched short calls (server-side batched RPC): Same accounting as above; tokens attributed per logical call. No hidden extra rounding beyond the model quantum.
- Nightly long-context jobs (30k context, 2k output): Invoice computation: base_window + additional_buckets = billed_context_buckets; total billed tokens = billed_context_buckets * bucket_size + outputs. Invoice line: ModelName context-buckets: N buckets -> $Z (or if on Dedicated: context_bucket_rate * N)

Attachments: I attached a short crosswalk PDF (redwood_billing_crosswalk.pdf) and an example SOW outline (SOW_redwood_finova_v2.docx). Vanessa, Tessa — can you review the per-bucket example numbers and confirm a sample invoice breakdown (we'll include line-level samples Jordan asked for)?

Next steps: 1) we'll send a one-page sample invoice with three lines (real-time, batched, nightly long-context) you can drop into your model; 2) propose a two-week committed pilot for the nightly job so we can give you a dedicated bucket rate to model.

Best,
Logan Wright
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Billing granularity mapping — internal calc notes

Logan / Tessa — quick calc notes for Jordan's examples (see attached spreadsheet). Quoting Jordan for context: 

On Thu, 02 Sep 2026 at 09:18 AM Jordan Meyers <jordan@finova.com> wrote:
> Our engineering team will do two things in production: (1) a high-volume real-time endpoint that streams short answers (mostly < 250 tokens output), and (2) a nightly batch job that runs expensive 30k-token context analyses over a corpus.

Example numbers (using conservative buckets):
- base_window = 8,192 tokens
- bucket_size = 2,048 tokens
- hosted quantum = 10 tokens (hosted payg rounding)

Nightly job: 30,000 context tokens -> billed_buckets = 1 + ceil((30,000 - 8,192)/2,048) = 1 + ceil(21,808/2,048) = 1 + 11 = 12 buckets.
Billed context tokens = 12 * 2,048 = 24,576 (note we bill buckets, not raw context length).
Output tokens (2,000) + context (24,576) -> reported billed tokens = 26,576.
If dedicated commitment applies, reduce per-bucket price by negotiated discount.

Real-time stream: 150 in + 70 out = 220 tokens per logical call -> apply hosted quantum rounding up to nearest 10 -> 220 -> invoice counts as 220 (already divisible by 10). If it were 223 tokens, we'd round to 230 for hosted quantum. For dedicated per-token SKUs, we would not round the same way — charges track exact tokens against commit until monthly reconciliation.

I'll draft a sample invoice using these numbers and attach it to Logan's reply.

— Vanessa
Director, Customer Solutions | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Billing granularity mapping — crosswalk for mixed real-time and batch requests (sample invoice attached)

Jordan — good questions. Short answers then attachments.

1) Cache / KV reuse credits: we give usage credit for internal prefix/KV reuse only in two cases: (a) when you enable rendered-response caching via the Optimize layer (explicit cache key + TTL) we apply caching credits that reduce billed tokens for hits; (b) for certain Dedicated plans we offer a KV-warmth credit that offsets repeated prefix costs during the same session window. Default hosted payg does not automatically credit raw token counts for model-side KV reuse (because the KV still occupies memory on the runtime); instead we optimize runtime cost and reflect savings in the rate card for committed customers.

2) Server-side batching reconciliation: yes. When you do server-side batching we still track attribution by logical request ID. You will get one invoice line for "real-time logical calls" showing total logical calls and aggregated tokens. We can include metadata fields (custom tags) so your billing ingestion can split lines by feature (we've done this in several integrations).

Attached is a 3-line sample invoice (PDF) using the example rates in your spreadsheet and our sample hosted/dedicated rates:
- Line 1: Real-time hosted calls (logical calls: 1,000, avg tokens/call: 220) -> Total tokens: 220,000 -> Rate: $0.0009/token -> Line total: $198.00
- Line 2: Nightly long-context (12 context buckets/day * 30 days = 360 buckets) -> bucket_size billed tokens: 360 * 2,048 = 737,280 -> output tokens: 2,000/day * 30 = 60,000 -> Total billed tokens: 797,280 -> Bucket rate (example dedicated discount): $0.0006/token-equivalent -> Line total: $478.37
- Line 3: Storage/retention/observability add-on (optional) -> monthly flat fee: $500

Those numbers are illustrative — final pricing will tie to the commitment level in the SOW. I've attached the sample invoice (redwood_billing_crosswalk.pdf) and the SOW outline. If Finova is comfortable with the mapping, let's schedule a 30-minute call next week to agree the committed bucket rate and finalize the SOW.
